title: The Local shop at the corner
subtitle: 社区社会 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）
meta: 主题语境：社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）　|　核心词汇：local　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 local 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1977 the operator wrote of ① a local shop at the corner in the log, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② so local that nobody in the station would go near it. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the operator, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the local ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the local shop at the corner that anybody there had ever seen, or so the log for June 1971 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too local to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the trainee who had come to help; the local ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a local news from the town, and said that no trainee in his right mind would call it ⑥ as local as the news from the town they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was local or not, and he said so.

By 1984 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was ⑦ something local, and nothing besides. The trainee from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite local; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the log kept the names of the local ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1987, in the rain, she wrote of another local shop at the corner in the same log, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ no less local than anybody had expected. ⑩ The local news from the town that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1989, was the one she could never quite name; the local ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 当地（前置定语 a local shop at the corner：1977 年操作员在运行日志里记下的那件当地的铺子）
B. adj. 当地／本地（两处加强说法：so local that … 与 no less local than …）
C. adj. 当地／本地（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 当地（表语 too local to do：母亲觉得它太当地，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 本地（前置定语 a local news from the town：叔叔把整件事称作一桩本地的消息）
F. adj. 本地（同级比较 as local as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩镇上的本地消息相比）
G. adj. 本地（后置定语 something local：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 本地（受程度副词修饰 quite local：那位实习生的评价）

items.q: a local shop at the corner
the local shop at the corner that
a local news from the town
The local news from the town that

answers.why: local 意为“当地”，1977 年操作员在运行日志里记下的是“一件当地的铺子”，此处作前置定语 a local shop at the corner。
local 意为“当地”，此处用 so local that 结构，说它当地到机房里没人敢靠近。
local 意为“当地”，运行日志上 六月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的当地街角本地人开的铺子，等于最高级的说法。
local 意为“当地”，母亲认为这件东西“太当地了，谁也用不上”，too local to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
local 意为“本地”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩本地的消息”，此处作前置定语 a local news from the town。
local 意为“本地”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩镇上的本地消息一样本地”，同级比较用 as local as。
local 意为“本地”，运行日志上那半行字要的是“本地的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something local。
local 意为“本地”，邻机房来的那位实习生认为这套计划“相当本地”，quite 修饰原级 local。
local 意为“本地”，no less local than 表示“其本地不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之本地不亚于任何人的预料。
local 意为“本地”，母亲 1989 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的本地消息”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1977 年，操作员在运行日志里记下了一件当地的铺子。（a local shop at the corner）
它当地到机房里没有一个人敢靠近。（so local that …）
母亲觉得它太当地，谁也用不上。（too local to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩本地的消息。（a local news from the town）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩镇上的本地消息一样本地。（as local as …）
到了 1984 年，运行日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件本地的东西。（something local）
answers: In 1977 the operator wrote of a local shop at the corner in the log.
It was so local that nobody in the station would go near it.
My mother thought it too local to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a local news from the town.
He said nobody would call it as local as the news from the town they had once had.
By 1984 the log asked for nothing but something local.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 local 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1977 the operator wrote of a local shop at the corner in the log, and nobody forgot it.
It was the local shop at the corner that anybody there had ever seen, or so the log says.
My mother thought it too local to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a local news from the town, and nobody argued with him.
The trainee from the next station called the plan quite local, and everybody laughed.
The local ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
